$comment: TURF (acoustic ceiling tiles, wall panels and baffles, owned by Armstrong World Industries) runs a Next.js site on Sanity with one page per product under /products/<name> (Slice, Petal, Voronoi, Peak, Step, Freeform). The product name is the h1, the description is the meta description and the image is og:image. TURF sells through designers and dealers, so there is no price: price and availability are not configured and every product returns price.state unknown with a PRICE_MISSING warning; price_unit usd only keeps currency USD. The acoustic rating (NRC) and felt specification are in the page's technical section, which the selectors do not read, so fetch.engine is default (APP_DEFAULT_ENGINE, ai-crawler-avalai on this instance): the LLM returns 2 specs (acoustic rating and felt specification) with the image and description, each checked against the page, at about 1,858+723 tokens per request. The live server fetch of the page times out with the http engine (plain HTTP), while headless Chrome gets it, so the AI page fetch is used. Engines tried on the sample on 2026-11-19: http: FETCH_TIMEOUT; browser: SUCCESS with title, image and description; ai-crawler-avalai: the same plus 2 specs. ai-crawler-avalai is selected because it returns the specs. Needs APP_AI_CRAWLER_ENABLED with an AvalAI key on the instance. Checked against the saved (curl) Slice product page on 2026-11-19.
